annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bulgaria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, and Sweden (submitted to CCW GGE on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.4)
named_instruments_referenced: Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions
annotation.summary_en: Working paper by eleven European states to the CCW GGE on LAWS arguing for "context-appropriate human judgement and control" as the core concept for ensuring IHL compliance of autonomous weapons across the system lifecycle, and urging the GGE to turn convergence into concrete instrument language before its 2026 mandate ends.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports framing LAWS governance as context-appropriate human judgement and control to comply with IHL.
Human judgement and control must be exercised across development (Art. 36 legal review, testing) and deployment (rules of engagement, spatial/temporal limits).
Direct, continuous human oversight is not required by IHL; prior control over mission parameters can suffice.
Context factors include system complexity, environment, civilian proximity and information reliability.
Calls on GGE members to convert convergence into concrete language before the 2026 mandate ends.
